Note::select¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::select(std::int64_t dim, std::int64_t index) const

Take One Slab Along An Axis And Drop That Axis¶

select(dim, index) returns the sub-Note at position index along axis dim, with that axis removed — so the result has one lower rank than the input. Selecting row 1 of a 2 × 3 grid gives a rank-1 Note of three cells; selecting an element of a rank-1 Note gives a 0-D scalar. Reach for it to pull a single row, column, or plane out of a grid by its index.

Nothing about the text changes: the picked cells are shared with the source, the bytes-vs-UTF-8 mode carries over, and the cost is one O(result numel) copy of the offset table.

The arguments¶

Argument

Meaning

dim

Which axis to index. 0 is the outermost. A negative value counts from the back: -1 is the last axis. After that adjustment it must be in [0, dim()), otherwise dim out of range.

index

The position along dim to keep. A negative value counts from the end of that axis: -1 is its last slab. After adjustment it must be in [0, size(dim)), otherwise select index out of range.

select needs at least one axis: on a 0-D scalar it raises dim out of range. To pick cells from a rank-1 Note by an arbitrary list of positions rather than one, use take; to keep a contiguous range along an axis without dropping it, use narrow.

Example 1: An Element Of A 1-D Note¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << v.select(0, 2) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"c"

The rank-1 Note becomes a 0-D scalar holding just "c".

Example 2: A Row And A Column Of A Grid¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.select(0, 1)) << "\n";   // row 1
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.select(1, 0)) << "\n";   // column 0

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["d", "e", "f"]
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a", "d"]

select(0, 1) keeps axis 1 (the columns) and drops axis 0; select(1, 0) keeps axis 0 (the rows) and drops axis 1.

Example 3: Negative dim And Negative index¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.select(-1, 2)) << "\n";   // last axis, last column

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << v.select(0, -1) << "\n";                       // last element

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["c", "f"]
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"f"

Example 4: Dropping The Middle Axis Of A Rank-3 Note¶

const auto t = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}).reshape({1, 2, 3});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(t.select(1, 0)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 3], dim=2, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "c"]
]

The 1 × 2 × 3 shape loses axis 1, leaving 1 × 3.

Example 5: Rejections¶

auto first_line = [](const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string m = e.what();
  return m.substr(0, m.find('\n'));
};

try { (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b"}).select(0, 5); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::make_note("x").select(0, 0); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

Output¶

select index out of range
dim out of range

A 0-D scalar has no axis 0 to select along.

See Also¶

  • Note::narrow: keep a contiguous range of slabs along an axis and keep the axis.

  • Note::take: gather cells by an arbitrary index list (rank-1 result).

  • Note::squeeze: drop a size-1 axis without indexing into it.
